$comment: AgentX reference topologies. Each shape is DESIGNED TO ALIGN WITH the blocking governance rules (IG-01..IG-05); these are design descriptions rather than IaC, so run the governance gate against the code you generate from them. Provider services are named generically so the shape ports across clouds.

topologies.intent: Stateless HTTP API with a relational store. The default shape for a CRUD prototype.
governanceNotes: Compute authenticates to database via managed identity (IG-01), no connection string literal (IG-02).
No gateway by default - add one only when you need routing, quotas, or key management.
Idle cost is near zero, which is what makes this the safest prototype default.
topologies.whenNotToUse: Long-running jobs, streaming workloads, or anything needing sub-second cold-start guarantees.

topologies.intent: Ingest, transform, and land events. Use when the workload is asynchronous.
governanceNotes: Dead-letter path is mandatory; silent message loss is the defining failure of this shape.
Function identity is granted least-privilege on the store (IG-01).
Cost scales with message volume - declare the volume assumption in the cost envelope (IG-09).
topologies.whenNotToUse: Synchronous user-facing requests that need an immediate response.

topologies.intent: Application grounded on an indexed corpus, backed by a model endpoint.
governanceNotes: The search index is usually an always-on floor - price it first, it often dominates.
Model endpoint keys must come from the secret store, never inline (IG-02).
Pair with the rag-pipelines and ai-evaluation skills for retrieval quality gates.
topologies.whenNotToUse: Corpora small enough to fit in a prompt, where an index adds cost and no accuracy.

topologies.intent: Browser UI plus a thin backend. The cheapest shape for a demo that needs a real UI.
governanceNotes: No always-on component - typically the lowest idle cost of any shape here.
Enforce auth at the API, never in client-side code alone.
Pairs with the working-prototype-app skill for the frontend build.
topologies.whenNotToUse: Server-rendered apps needing per-request server state or long-lived connections.

topologies.intent: Multi-service internal tool where a gateway genuinely earns its cost.
governanceNotes: The gateway is an always-on floor and will dominate a low-traffic bill - justify it explicitly.
Adopt only when you need central auth, rate limiting, or a stable external contract.
For a single service, request-response-api is materially cheaper.
topologies.whenNotToUse: Single-service prototypes, where the gateway is pure overhead.
